fields.why: Median length of stay appears only as a Table row and no claim in the text rests on it; the brief lists only the types the claims rest on.
The Table note states 'Data are not presented for cells with sample size <10', and the brief names suppression of observed values as a transformation (ancillary here).

Methods state the rates were used to 'compare these rates with those from previous surveillance periods', and Figure 1 and the Results compare October–April seasons since 2020–2021. A recorded season in comparison.across but not the design.

The chart abstraction is COVID-NET's own data-collection step, so it can be read as part of the network or as a separate record source. A rule such as 'a network's internal chart abstraction is subsumed under sentinel/network' would decide it.

The article quantifies vaccine receipt among hospitalized adults (88.1% unvaccinated with the 2023–2024 dose, in the Summary), which reads as uptake. It is equally defensible as a case characteristic outside the primary question (null).
Sex is a Table stratum and the brief says age and sex are 'recorded always', so B missed it. A's 'other' for LTCF residence is a care setting framed as clinical risk, not a social position.

The only explanation offered is the racial and ethnic disparity in vaccination coverage, a health-service factor rather than a social, structural or political determinant. Both readers already agree it does not raise the level to 4.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether a sentinel network's own medical-record abstraction is also 'record abstraction or interview', or whether vaccination status among cases (not a population) counts toward vaccine_outcome_type coverage/uptake.
